name_note: A large share of the genomes in this GTDB genus carry the NCBI name Butyricicoccus, consistent with a published genome-scale transfer of Butyricicoccus faecihominis into Agathobaculum.

sentences.text: Agathobaculum was described from strain SR79, isolated from a Korean faecal sample: a strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile short rod producing butyric acid as a major end product.
The genus sits in the family Oscillospiraceae, a group of prominent anaerobic gut bacteria that includes many butyrate producers.
A genome-scale reassessment found Butyricicoccus faecihominis closely related to Agathobaculum members and transferred it into this genus.
Agathobaculum massiliense, a Gram-stain-negative, non-motile, non-spore-forming rod, was isolated from the stool of a healthy donor.
In mouse experiments, Agathobaculum butyriciproducens SR79 has been reported to improve cognition and reduce Alzheimer's disease pathology.
